This is a retype-the-residual move (Reflection 225 family: the sorry's *type* changed from an unprovable proposition to a provable one — that retype is the progress, even though the sorry count is unchanged at 4), but with a sharper lesson than 225's "wire in a consumer": **when a deferred goal is universally quantified and has lived only as a hypothesis, spend the few minutes to construct a witness/counterexample before investing in its proof.** The probe cost five lines and one `#eval`; producing the false goal would have cost an unbounded number of sessions chasing a `content_start` that cannot hold. Sits with [[ref-reduction-by-import]] (retype-not-shrink) and the [[ref-producer-guarded-quantifier]] trap (a quantifier whose guard is missing is undischargeable yet type-checks) — this is that same trap one level up: not a *premise* inside one lemma, but the *target structure* of the entire frontier.

### Reflection 230 (new, 2026-06-02): an "array wrapper" lemma silently encodes its window as *to-the-array-end*; generalizing it to a bounded `[lo, hi)` window is the cheap, mechanical brick that unblocks every nested-subrange consumer — and the bound only needs a prefix-coincidence lemma, not a re-proof

With `FlowSubrangesOk` guarded and provable (Reflection 229), the next step was producing the seq subrange primitives. Tracing the outer-span derivation showed it does NOT lift for free (it is entangled with the `s₂.filter p` push decomposition, not a clean `SafeBody` hypothesis), and the genuine substrate — `SafeBody_array_flowEntry` / `SafeBodyUnit_array_succ`, the array wrappers that turn a list-level `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit` into the `after_fe` / value-end-successor token facts — is stated over `arr.toList.drop lo`, i.e. the body window runs *to the end of the array*. That is exactly right for the OUTER span (whose body is everything between the boundary brackets, ending two before the array end) and exactly WRONG for a nested subrange `[lo, hi)`, whose body ends at `hi < size` with more outer structure after it. The "array wrapper" had silently baked the outer-span window into its type. The fix is the bounded variant `SafeBody_array_flowEntry_window` / `SafeBodyUnit_array_succ_window` over `(arr.toList.take hi).drop lo`, and the lesson is how *cheap* it is: the entire delta between the unbounded and windowed proofs is one helper, `window_prefix_eq` — the balance-relevant prefix `[lo, k)` of the windowed body is *the same list* as the unbounded `drop lo` prefix whenever the cut `k ≤ hi` (both name elements `[lo, k)`; proved by `List.ext_getElem` + `simp [getElem_take, getElem_drop]`). Given that coincidence, the *list-level* lemmas (`SafeBody_flowEntry_zero_balance`, `SafeBodyUnit_succ`) — which never cared about the window — apply unchanged to the windowed list, `flowBracketBalance_eq_pbalance` connects the array balance to it, and the only difference in the conclusion is the close bound sharpening from `k+1 < size` to `k+1 < hi`. No combinatorics re-proved; the bound is pure list-slice algebra. Two lessons compound. (1) **Diagnostic:** when a lemma is named `_array`/`_offset`/"wrapper", suspect it has hard-coded *which* window — read its body slice (`drop lo` vs `(take hi).drop lo`) before assuming it applies to a nested instance; an outer-span wrapper is not a subrange wrapper. (2) **Method:** to generalize a window, do not re-walk the inductive proof — find the prefix/slice-coincidence that lets the *existing* (windowed-agnostic) core lemma fire, and transport. This sits with [[ref-parametric-assembler-extraction]] (lift fixed-span facts to `∀ lo hi`; the symmetric second wrapper — the `SafeBodyUnit` dual — was indeed fresh-but-cheap once the `SafeBody` one and the shared `window_prefix_eq` existed) and is the substrate half of the seq-primitive residual: the wrappers are the joint the recursive *producer* of the windowed `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit` will call once it has them — which is now the narrowed Phase-J frontier.

### Reflection 231 (new, 2026-06-02): build the *consumer joint* before the producer — a single lemma keyed only on the recursion's deliverable collapses an entire side's assembly to one typed boundary, so the remaining work is exactly one shape, not a scatter of primitives

Last session landed the windowed array wrappers (Reflection 230); the obvious next step was "produce the windowed `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit`" — the recursion. But that recursion is large and not landable green in one session, so the question was what *self-contained* brick advances it. The answer was to look in the other direction: **build the consumer joint first.** `seqBodyProps_of_windowed_safebody` is a single lemma that takes the recursion's eventual *deliverable* — the windowed `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit ContentStartTok ((tokens.toList.take hi).drop lo)` plus the content-start head, as bare hypotheses — together with the balanced-subrange facts, and produces the full `SeqBodyProps tokens lo hi`. Its proof is pure plumbing already in hand: drive `SafeBody_array_flowEntry_window` and `SafeBodyUnit_array_succ_window` (Reflection 230) into `seqBodyProps_assemble` (Reflection 226), with the only glue being the `getElem!`↔`getElem` bridge (`getElem!_pos`; the wrappers conclude over `arr[k]'_` while the assembler primitives are stated over `tokens[k]!`) and the definitional `ContentStartTok = isFlowContentStart` (`exact` sees through both `def`s). Fully provable now, axiom-clean, no new sorry.

**The value is what it does to the residual's *shape*, not the sorry count** (the [[ref-reduction-by-import]] family — wiring a consumer retypes the residual; the retype is the progress). Before this lemma, the seq-side residual was a scatter: produce three primitives (content-start, value-end successor, post-`.flowEntry` content-start) AND assemble them. After it, the seq-side residual is *exactly one shape*: produce the windowed `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit` + content-start head at a nested guarded subrange — feed it to `seqBodyProps_of_windowed_safebody`, done. Everything between "I have the windowed SafeBody" and "I have `FlowSubrangesOk.seq`" is now a single proven call. This is the mirror discipline to building the producer: when the producer is the hard recursion, build the *consumer* of its not-yet-existing output first — it costs nothing now (the plumbing already exists), it cannot regress (it is fully proven), and it forces the recursion's interface to a single named type. The next session's target stops being "the seq primitives" (which invites re-deriving the assembly each time) and becomes one crisp deliverable: `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit` over the windowed slice. Note the asymmetry with the map side — there is no `mapBodyProps_of_windowed_safebody` yet, because a map *pair* is not a single `EntryUnit` (interior depth-0 `.value`), so its consumer joint needs the pair-level alternation primitives, not one windowed `SafeBody`; that joint is a separate (fresh-but-cheap, once the seq one exists) brick. Sits with [[ref-parametric-assembler-extraction]] (the assembler was the *assemble* half; this is the *adapt-the-substrate-to-the-assembler* half) and [[ref-array-wrapper-window-generalization]] (whose wrappers this lemma is the first consumer of).

### Reflection 232 (new, 2026-06-02): the symmetric "mirror" joint can be asymmetric in *yield* even when symmetric in *form* — the same `SafeBody` machinery applies on both sides, but what it discharges is bounded by the grammar's depth structure, not by the lemma shape

Reflection 231 predicted the map-side consumer joint as "a separate (fresh-but-cheap, once the seq one exists) brick … because a map *pair* is not a single `EntryUnit`." Building it this session (commit `6cae8b14`) confirmed the cost but sharpened the *reason* — and the sharpening is the lesson. The map producer `emitPairList_scans_safebody` does deliver a *single* windowed inductive: `SafeBody (· = .key) block` — not the eight scattered primitives I'd feared. So `mapBodyProps_of_windowed_safebody` *is* a clean mirror of the seq joint in **form**: same `refine mapBodyProps_assemble … ?_ ?_ …`, same `SafeBody.head_Q` for the head, same `SafeBody_array_flowEntry_window` (which is already generic in `Q`, so `Q := (· = .key)` fires with zero new machinery), same `getElem!`↔`getElem` glue. The lemma practically wrote itself from the seq one. **But its yield is smaller, and the gap is structural, not accidental.** The seq joint discharged the full residual (its `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit` deliverable produces *every* extra `seqBodyProps_assemble` primitive); the map joint discharges only the two **body-boundary** primitives — M1 `key_start` (the body head is a `.key`) and M2 `after_fe` (after a depth-0 `.flowEntry`, a `.key`). The six **pair-interior** primitives (key→content, key→value, value→content, value→successor, the two value-close bracket successors) are *invisible to the `SafeBody`*, because `SafeBody Q` splits the body only at depth-0 `.flowEntry` separators and treats each whole pair `.key block_k .value block_v` as one `EntrySafe` entry — the interior depth-0 `.value` (the key/value boundary) lives *below* the `SafeBody`'s resolution. The same machine sees the pair boundaries and is blind to the pair internals, purely because a YAML flow-map's two depth-0 delimiters (`,` between pairs, `:` within a pair) sit at the *same* bracket depth but the inductive only branches on one of them. **General principle: when you build the symmetric counterpart of a successful brick, do not assume symmetric *payoff* — a shared abstraction (here `SafeBody Q`) discharges exactly the obligations that live at *its* granularity, and a richer grammar on the other side pushes some obligations below that granularity where the same lemma cannot reach them.** The mirror is still worth building — it is free (the seq plumbing generalizes verbatim), it cannot regress, and it collapses the *boundary* half of the map residual onto the producer's natural single deliverable, so the next session's map target is "produce the windowed `SafeBody (· = .key)` + the six interior pair primitives" rather than "produce eight scattered primitives." But the honest accounting is that the map producer must still expose pair-interior structure the seq producer never needed — the asymmetry the grammar forced (Reflection 228's "eight premises vs three") reappears here as a *coverage* gap in the otherwise-identical joint. Sits with [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (this is its map-side instance, with the caveat made precise) and [[ref-parametric-assembler-extraction]]'s "symmetric second lemma is fresh-but-cheap" — cheap to *write*, yes, but the symmetry stops at the lemma boundary; the obligations it leaves open are set by the grammar, not the proof.

### Reflection 233 (new, 2026-06-02): before building a large producer, prove its *contract is satisfiable* at the boundary case the consumer abstraction structurally cannot represent — the de-risking step is to check that the case your machine can't cover is the case it is never asked to cover

The frontier had converged on one large piece: produce the nested-subrange `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit` that both consumer joints ([[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]]) consume. Asked how to scope the session, the user chose **"de-risk first"** over committing to the recursion — and the de-risk paid for itself by exposing a structural gap that, left unexamined, would have surfaced as an unprovable obligation deep inside the producer. The consumer joints are keyed on `SafeBody`, an inductive with **no `nil` constructor**: it cannot represent an *empty* body. And empty bodies are not hypothetical — `emit (.sequence … #[]) = "[]"` and `emit (.mapping … #[]) = "{}"` (the emitter's literal definition: `emitList [] = ""`), so a value like `[[], "a"]` scans to a nested `[` immediately followed by `]`, i.e. an interior `[lo, hi)` with `lo = hi`, and `FlowSubrangesOk.seq`/`.map` (quantifying over `lo ≤ hi`) genuinely reaches it. So the `SafeBody`-keyed architecture has a case it *structurally cannot* handle. The question that decides whether the architecture is sound: **is that case one the producer must discharge with a `SafeBody`, or one it can discharge another way?** Reading the target contract answered it cleanly: every field of `SeqBodyProps`/`MapBodyProps` is guarded — the head fields (`content_start`/`key_start`) by `lo < hi`, all the rest by `∀ k, lo ≤ k → k < hi` — so at `lo = hi` *every field is vacuous*. The empty case needs no `SafeBody` at all; `seqBodyProps_empty`/`mapBodyProps_empty` close it with a `subst` and an anonymous constructor of `omega`-closed vacuous fields (axiom-clean `[propext, Quot.sound]`, no `Classical.choice`). So the producer's contract **splits cleanly along `lo < hi`**: the empty branch is the leaf lemmas (no `SafeBody`), the nonempty branch is the consumer joints — and crucially the nonempty branch is *exactly* where `emitList_scans_safebody`'s `items ≠ []` precondition is met, so the recursion is well-typed precisely where it is invoked. The architecture is SOUND: the one case the consumer abstraction cannot represent is the one case it is never asked to cover, and the two coincide *by the guard structure of the target*, not by luck. The general lesson, dual to [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] (probe whether a universal is *true* before producing it): before building a large producer onto a consumer abstraction, identify the boundary case that abstraction *cannot represent*, then check the target contract — if the contract is *vacuous* there, the abstraction is sound and you've earned a cheap green leaf lemma; if the contract demands real content there, you've found a hole *before* sinking a session into a recursion that would dead-end at it. The de-risk is not a detour from the producer — it is the producer's base case, found by asking where the chosen machine breaks and whether the spec breaks with it. Sits with [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (the joints are sound only because this leaf complements them) and [[ref-converse-forward-invariant-asymmetry]] (the empty body is the degenerate inductive the forward construction omits).

### Reflection 234 (new, 2026-06-02): when the consumer's flat invariant cannot carry what the descent needs, the producer's deliverable must be a *recursive* type — define it and prove it projects to the flat form FIRST, so wiring it collapses a scattered "do X at every nesting level" residual into one boundary

The seq-side `lo < hi` branch needs a windowed `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit` at *every* nested guarded subrange — not just the outer body (which `emitList_scans_safebody` already delivers). The instinct is to produce the flat `SafeBody` at each subrange by a token-level recursion. That instinct hits a wall the moment you check it: **`SafeBody → WellBracketed` is FALSE.** `SafeBody`'s per-entry obligation `EntrySafe` constrains the running balance *only at `.flowEntry` positions* (they must sit at depth ≥ 1); it says nothing about a non-`.flowEntry` prefix, which could dip negative. That is exactly why the emit producers carry `WellBracketed` as a *separate* conjunct rather than reading it off the `SafeBody` — the flat invariant is too weak to regenerate the bracket structure a descent into a nested entry's interior would need. So a flat deliverable cannot be the producer's output: to hand the descent-locator a nested entry's interior as a `SafeBody`, that interior's structure must already be *recorded*, not re-derived. The fix is to make the deliverable a **recursive type**: `RecSeqBody`/`RecSeqEntry` (mutual inductives) is a `SafeBody` over `ContentStartTok` that additionally carries, at each nested flow-sequence entry, its interior's own `RecSeqBody` (the `seq` constructor's `h_rec`); leaves (`scalar`), empties (`seqEmpty`), and — for now — nested mappings (`map`, bottoming out at `WellBracketed`, the map recursion deferred to a `RecMapBody` brick) close the recursion. The discipline that makes this a safe brick rather than speculative scaffolding: **prove the flat projection FIRST.** `RecSeqBody.toSafeBody`/`.toSafeBodyUnit` discharge to exactly the windowed `SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit ContentStartTok` the consumer joint `seqBodyProps_of_windowed_safebody` already consumes, via the per-entry `RecSeqEntry.toEntrySafe`/`.toEntryUnit` (`wrap_{seq,map}_block`'s `EntrySafe` half / `EntryUnit_wrap` for bracket entries, `EntrySafe_scalar`/`EntryUnit_scalar` for leaves) — and those projections use *only* `WellBracketed`, never the recursive `h_rec`, so they are robust to the map bottoming-out and to any later constructor tweak. Two mechanical notes that cost real minutes: (1) a doc comment `/-- … -/` cannot precede `mutual` (parser rejects it) — use a section comment `/-! … -/`; (2) `induction` is *rejected* on a mutual inductive ("does not support … mutually inductive") — write the projection as term-mode structural recursion (`| _, .single … => …  | _, .cons … h_rest => … h_rest.toSafeBody`), which the equation compiler accepts because it recurses only on the `RecSeqBody` argument (the entry is handled by the non-recursive `toEntrySafe`). (3) A recursive occurrence cannot sit under `Or` ("invalid nested inductive datatype 'Or'"), so the empty-interior case is a *separate* constructor (`seqEmpty`) rather than `interior = [] ∨ RecSeqBody interior`. The payoff is the [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] reshape lifted one nesting level: defining `RecSeqBody` as the producer's output type collapses the scattered residual "produce a flat windowed `SafeBody` at *every* nested subrange" into the single typed boundary "produce *one* `RecSeqBody` of the outer body," to be split downstream by the descent-locator (`RecSeqBody` → windowed `SafeBody` at any subrange) and supplied upstream by strengthening `emitList_scans_safebody` (its per-item `ih` supplies each `seq` entry's `h_rec`). Build green 525 jobs, sorries held at 4, all four lemmas axiom-clean `[propext, Quot.sound]`. The general lesson: when a descent will need to treat sub-parts the same way it treats the whole, but the flat invariant the consumer is keyed on cannot regenerate a sub-part's structure (here `SafeBody ↛ WellBracketed`), the producer must deliver a *recursive* witness — and the way to land that safely in one increment, without committing to the producer or the descent yet, is to define the recursive type and prove it *projects to the flat form the consumer already accepts*, so the type is validated from both ends before either hard half is attempted. Sits with [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (this is its recursive generalization — the joint consumes the *projection*, the descent consumes the *recursion*) and [[ref-derisk-consumer-blindspot-vs-contract]] (there the consumer abstraction's blind spot was the empty body; here it is the *flatness* — `SafeBody` forgets the nesting, and the deliverable must remember it).

### Reflection 235 (new, 2026-06-02): land the irreducible single-level step of a recursive descent FIRST, and let its conclusion type be the producer-contract split you already proved — the case analysis on the deliverable's constructors recovers the recursion witness and rules out the impossible shapes, so the step is fully provable before the positional bridge or the outer recursion exist

With the recursive deliverable `RecSeqBody` defined and projected (Reflection 234), the descent-locator — "from `RecSeqBody (outer body)`, extract a windowed `SafeBody` at *any* nested guarded subrange" — is still a multi-session brick: it needs a positional bridge (a guarded subrange `[lo,hi)` with `tokens[lo-1]` an opener ↔ which `RecSeqEntry` of the windowed body) and an outer recursion composing the per-level steps. But the *irreducible atom* of that recursion — "descend one nesting level" — is fully provable now, in isolation, and is the right thing to land first. `RecSeqEntry.seq_interior` takes a `RecSeqEntry e` and the bracket-entry shape `e = op :: (interior ++ [cl])` with `op.val = .flowSequenceStart`, and `cases` on the four constructors: `scalar` (`e = [t]`) forces `interior ++ [cl] = []`, impossible; `map` has a `.flowMappingStart` head clashing with `.flowSequenceStart`; `seqEmpty` gives `interior = []`; `seq` gives the recursive `h_rec : RecSeqBody interior'` with `interior' = interior` (read off the constructor index by `append_singleton_inj`, a core-Lean `a ++ [x] = b ++ [y] → a = b ∧ x = y` proved by `reverse` + `List.reverse_inj`). The thing that makes this clean rather than a fight: **its conclusion type is chosen to be the producer-contract split you already proved.** The output is `RecSeqBody interior ∨ interior = []` — and that is *exactly* the `lo < hi` / `lo = hi` dichotomy of Reflection 233. The non-empty disjunct feeds `seqBodyProps_of_windowed_safebody` (via `RecSeqBody.toSafeBody`); the empty disjunct routes to `seqBodyProps_empty`. So the single-level step doesn't merely descend — it descends *into the shape the next stage already consumes*, both branches included, with no leftover obligation. The map mirror `RecSeqEntry.map_interior` is even tighter: a `.flowMappingStart`-headed entry yields `WellBracketed interior` (no disjunction — the map interior bottoms out at its bracket substrate, `WellBracketed []` covering the empty case too), so the descent into a nested *mapping* hands the map consumer joint exactly its bracket fact with no recursion, deferring the key/value recursion to the map-side `RecMapBody` brick. The general lesson, a sequencing rule for recursive descents: don't wait for the positional bridge and the outer recursion to be designed before proving anything — the **single-level constructor case-split is self-contained** (the deliverable's constructors *are* the case analysis: the wanted recursion witness falls out of one constructor, the impossible shapes are killed by the head/shape mismatch), so land it first, and pick its conclusion type to be the split the downstream stage already expects, so the atom plugs in with zero glue when the recursion is later assembled. Build green 523 jobs, sorries held at 4, all three lemmas (`append_singleton_inj`, `seq_interior`, `map_interior`) axiom-clean `[propext]`. Sits with [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] and [[ref-derisk-consumer-blindspot-vs-contract]] (the descent step's two output disjuncts are the joint's `lo < hi` input and the de-risk's `lo = hi` leaf — the step routes each subrange to whichever was already built) and [[ref-recursive-deliverable-project-to-flat-first]] (this consumes the recursive type that reflection defined; the flat projection it proved is what the non-empty disjunct composes with).

### Reflection 236 (new, 2026-06-02): a recursive descent's positional bridge splits into a *slice* half (pure list arithmetic) and a *locate* half (balance↔structure) — land the slice half NOW; it is self-contained, reuses the single-level step's glue, and reduces the descent to "located interior → consumer" so only the genuinely analytical locate remains

The single-level descent step (Reflection 235) recovers a nested entry's interior as a `List` (`RecSeqEntry.seq.h_rec : RecSeqBody interior`). But the consumer joint `seqBodyProps_of_windowed_safebody` is keyed on the *positionally windowed* form `(tokens.toList.take hi).drop lo` — a slice of the token array, not an abstract list. Bridging the two is the descent-locator's **positional bridge**, and the temptation is to treat it as one monolith that needs balance reasoning (which entry of the body does a guarded subrange `[lo,hi)` select?). It is not a monolith — it cleanly *factors*: (a) a **slice** half — "given that the array window `(tokens.toList.take (hi+1)).drop lo` *equals* a bracket entry's `interior ++ [cl]`, conclude `interior = (tokens.toList.take hi).drop lo`" — and (b) a **locate** half — "which entry of the windowed outer body does `[lo,hi)`'s `tokens[lo-1]` opener select, and why is its `interior` exactly that window." Only (b) needs balance↔structure correspondence; (a) is pure list/array slicing. So (a) is fully provable *now*, before (b) is designed, and it is worth landing first: `interior_window_eq` peels the last element `tokens[hi]` off `take (hi+1)` (`List.take_add_one` + `List.getElem?_eq_getElem`), pushes the `drop lo` inside the resulting append (`List.drop_append_of_le_length`, discharged by `lo ≤ hi = |take hi|`), and reads `interior` off the trailing-singleton equation with the *same* `append_singleton_inj` the single-level step already used — no new machinery. The reusable principle, beyond this instance: **when you package per-element results into a universally-quantified consumer structure, check the structure's per-field hypotheses against what each element's proof actually needs — the difference is real and is exactly the producer's per-element deliverable; bundle that difference as a named type, point the assembler at it, and you have collapsed the whole packaging step into the producer's contract without yet writing the producer.** With this the consumer side is complete end-to-end including the locate boundary, and the entire remaining frontier is the two producers — the locate recursion delivering `SeqLocated`/`MapLocated` (fed by the emit-producer strengthening that delivers the top-level `RecSeqBody`/`RecMapBody`) — and the two base `content_eq` sorries. Sits with [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (the same build-the-consumer-first discipline, here at the universal-packaging boundary, keyed on the locate's bundled deliverable) and [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (`SeqLocated`/`MapLocated` are additive, depend only on already-defined pieces, and are the locate's deliverable contract just as `RecMapEntry` was the map front-end's).

### Reflection 244 (new, 2026-06-03): when a newly-added deliverable type joins the family, complete its *projection family* before the producer walks it — the omitted projection is the navigation invariant the locate needs *at that type's nesting level*, and it is a verbatim mirror of the sibling type's, not new analysis

R242 added the recursive map-entry deliverable `RecMapEntry` (`mapEmpty` / `map`-with-`RecMapBody`) and its single-level descent `RecMapEntry.map_interior`, but stopped there — the type joined the family with only the *descent* lemma, not its *projection* lemma. Every other type in the recursive-deliverable family carries a **balance projection** to `WellBracketed`: `RecSeqEntry.toWellBracketed` and `RecSeqBody.toWellBracketed` (R238), `RecMapPair.toWellBracketed` and `RecMapBody.toWellBracketed` (R240). R238 established *why* that projection is not optional decoration: it is the **navigation invariant the structural locate needs at every nesting level** — matching a guarded balanced subrange to an entry is a balance argument (the matching close of a depth-0 opener is the entry's last token), and descending into a nested entry's interior needs *that interior's own* `WellBracketed`, which only the deliverable's per-sub-part structure can supply, never a single global hypothesis. `RecMapEntry` is exactly the type the map locate's `MapLocated.entry` field holds, so the map locate will match a window to a `RecMapEntry` and needs *its* `WellBracketed` at the entry level — the same role `RecSeqEntry.toWellBracketed` plays for the seq locate. So the certain on-path next brick is `RecMapEntry.toWellBracketed`, and it is a **verbatim mirror** of `RecSeqEntry.toWellBracketed`'s map case, not new reasoning: both `RecMapEntry` constructors are `{ … }` frames, so `wrap_map_block` wraps the interior's `WellBracketed` (`WellBracketed_nil` for the `mapEmpty` `{}` leaf; `RecMapBody.toWellBracketed h_rec` for the non-empty `map` interior — the recursive sibling projection R240 already proved) and its `.1` is the entry's `WellBracketed`. Six lines, one `cases`. Verified-but-unconsumed (R225): references no sorry site, so the frontier sorry count is unchanged at 4. Build green 526 jobs; `RecMapEntry.toWellBracketed` axiom-clean (`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, no `sorryAx`). The reusable discipline, generalizing R238/R240: a recursive-deliverable family has *two* per-type obligations — the **descent** (one nesting level down, the producer-contract split) and the **projection** (the navigation invariant at this level). When a new member is added to satisfy a consumer joint (R242 added `RecMapEntry` for the map front-end), it tends to arrive with only the descent lemma the joint forced; **complete its projection family immediately**, before the producer walks it, because (i) it is the locate's navigation invariant at that member's level, owed regardless, (ii) it is a verbatim mirror of the sibling type's projection (its interior is another family member whose projection already exists), so it costs no analysis, and (iii) landing it now means the locate, when written, finds every type in the family already equipped at every level — no projection gap discovered mid-recursion. One caveat worth recording: the *typing* projection (`→ WellTyped`) is **not** available the same way — `RecSeqEntry.map`/`RecMapEntry` store only the interior's `WellBracketed`, not its `WellTyped` (the map interior was deliberately bottomed out at the untyped balance), so `WellTyped` would require a structural edit to the types (forbidden, [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]]); the locate's `.wt` field is instead recovered *positionally* from the outer window's `WellTyped` via `WellTyped_subrange`, not from a projection. So "complete the projection family" means complete the projections the *stored* fields support — here `WellBracketed`, not `WellTyped`. Sits with [[ref-recursive-deliverable-project-to-flat-first]] (the projection family validates the recursive type and equips the descent) and [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (`RecMapEntry` is the additive type whose family is now complete; the `WellTyped` caveat is exactly why no shared edit is taken).

### Reflection 245 (new, 2026-06-03): build the producer's per-level final-assembly step as the constructive dual of the consumer joint — when the consumer-side bridge that *reads* a deliverable off a window is already proven, its *write* direction is a free, verified-but-unconsumed brick that reduces the producer's deliverable by one structural layer

The Phase-J consumer side is closed end-to-end: `flowSubrangesOk_of_locators` (R243) reduces the universal residual `FlowSubrangesOk tokens` to the two per-window locator deliverables `SeqLocated`/`MapLocated`, and the whole family of `*_of_located_entry` / `*_of_recseqbody_window` joints (R236/R237) *consumes* a located `RecSeqEntry`/`RecMapEntry` and assembles the per-window `SeqBodyProps`/`MapBodyProps`. What is left is purely the **producer** — the locate recursion that *delivers* `SeqLocated`/`MapLocated` at every guarded window — together with the emit-producer strengthening that feeds it a top-level `RecSeqBody`/`RecMapBody`. Both are large mutual recursions, not one-session work; the question is what *certain on-path brick* lands green now.

The answer this session: the locate's **per-level final-assembly step**, `located_entry_of_recseqbody`, and the observation that it is the exact **constructive dual** of an already-proven *consumer* lemma. `seqBodyProps_of_located_entry` (R236, the front-end consumer) *reads* a located `RecSeqEntry ((take (hi+1)).drop (lo-1))` off the opener-window: it peels the opener (`List.getElem_cons_drop`, using `1 ≤ lo`), decomposes the rest (`List.take_add_one` + `List.drop_append_of_le_length`), and descends via `seq_interior`. The locate must go the *other* way — it has, from its inductive descent, the inner-window `RecSeqBody ((take hi).drop lo)`, and must *produce* the located `RecSeqEntry` of the opener-window (precisely `SeqLocated.entry`). That is the *same* positional bridge run constructively: the identical rest-decomposition and opener-peel lemmas put the absolute opener-window into the `op :: (interior ++ [cl])` shape `RecSeqEntry.seq` produces, and the recursive `RecSeqBody` supplies both the constructor's `WellBracketed interior` (via the R238 projection `RecSeqBody.toWellBracketed` — redundant with `h_rec` but the field demands it) and the `h_rec` field itself. It costs essentially nothing (the slicing already exists, copied verbatim from the consumer lemma), cannot regress (references no sorry site — verified-but-unconsumed, R225; the frontier sorry count holds at 4), and it **reduces the seq-side `SeqLocated` deliverable by one structural layer**: from "produce the located entry" to "produce the inner-window `RecSeqBody`" (plus the `pos`/`dyck`/`wt` bracket fields, which the window guards and `WellTyped_subrange` supply). The inner-window `RecSeqBody` is exactly the recursive obligation the locate descends on, so this brick names the locate's recursive boundary precisely while discharging its non-recursive packaging. Build green 527 jobs; `located_entry_of_recseqbody` axiom-clean (`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, no `sorryAx`).

The reusable discipline, the producer-side complement of the consumer-joint-before-producer family (R231/236/237/243): when you have already proven the consumer bridge that *reads* a deliverable off a positionally-windowed slice, its **write direction is a separate, immediately-landable brick** — same slicing lemmas, opposite direction, terminated by the deliverable type's constructor instead of its eliminator. Build it before the recursion, because it (i) is the recursion's per-level *final-assembly* step, owed regardless, (ii) reuses the consumer lemma's positional plumbing verbatim, so it costs no new analysis, and (iii) peels the non-recursive packaging off the deliverable, leaving the producer's residual as *exactly* the recursive sub-deliverable (`RecSeqBody` of the inner window) — the cleanest possible statement of what the recursion must still produce. The symmetric **map mirror** `located_mapentry_of_recmapbody` (producing `MapLocated.entry : RecMapEntry ((take (hi+1)).drop (lo-1))` from the inner-window `RecMapBody`, via the map peel/decompose and `RecMapEntry.map`) is the fresh-but-cheap next brick — a verbatim mirror over the map opener/closer kinds and the R244 `RecMapEntry` constructor, with the same caveat that `MapLocated`'s six pair-interior fields and `pos`/`dyck`/`wt` are supplied separately, not by this entry assembler. See [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (the consumer side this duals against), [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (the map mirror lands on R244's `RecMapEntry`), and [[ref-reduction-by-import]] (verified-but-unconsumed: retypes the residual one layer down, does not shrink the count).

### Reflection 246 (new, 2026-06-03): the symmetric mirror of a producer-dual is *not* a verbatim copy — its constructor call sheds exactly the fields the additive parallel type chose not to store, so the dual's arity reads R244's stored-vs-projected split right off the constructor signature

Reflection 245 predicted the map mirror `located_mapentry_of_recmapbody` as the fresh-but-cheap next brick — "a verbatim mirror over the map opener/closer kinds and the R244 `RecMapEntry` constructor." It landed this session exactly so for the **positional plumbing** (the `h_rest` rest-decomposition and `h_peel` opener-peel blocks are copied character-for-character from `located_entry_of_recseqbody`, only the bracket kinds `.flowSequenceStart`/`.flowSequenceEnd` → `.flowMappingStart`/`.flowMappingEnd` change), confirming the producer-dual discipline transports across the additive parallel type with zero new analysis. Build green **528 jobs**, frontier sorries held at **4**, `located_mapentry_of_recmapbody` axiom-clean (`[propext, Quot.sound]` — even cleaner than the seq sibling, which carried `Classical.choice`).

But the **constructor call is *not* verbatim**, and the one place it differs is itself the lesson. The seq dual closes with `RecSeqEntry.seq _ _ _ h_op_val h_cl_val h_rec.toWellBracketed h_rec` — *seven* arguments, the sixth being the `WellBracketed interior` the `RecSeqEntry.seq` constructor **stores** as a field, supplied via the R238 projection. The map dual closes with `RecMapEntry.map _ _ _ h_op_val h_cl_val h_rec` — *six* arguments, **no** `WellBracketed` among them, because `RecMapEntry.map` (R242's additive type) was deliberately built to store only the recursive `RecMapBody` and **project** its balance post-hoc via `RecMapEntry.toWellBracketed` (R244), rather than carry it at construction. So the mirror's *final-assembly line shrinks by exactly one argument*, and that argument is precisely the field R244's stored-vs-projected distinction says the parallel type does not store. The reusable point: **when you mirror a producer-dual onto an additive parallel type, do not assume the constructor application transports verbatim — read the parallel type's constructor signature first, because its arity differs from the sibling's by exactly the fields R242/R244 chose to internalize-and-project rather than store, and those are the arguments the dual's terminal `exact` must drop (or, on the other side, add).** The positional plumbing is symmetric; the constructor is symmetric only up to each type's storage decisions, and those decisions are visible — and only visible — at the terminal constructor line. With this, the map side's `MapLocated.entry` is reduced one structural layer (to the inner-window `RecMapBody`) exactly as the seq side was, and **both** per-level entry-assembly steps of the locate are now discharged; the remaining Phase-J producer residual is the seq/map locate recursion itself (delivering `SeqLocated`/`MapLocated`) fed by the emit-producer strengthening, then the two base `content_eq` sorries. See [[ref-producer-dual-of-consumer-joint]] (the dual discipline this completes the symmetric pair of), [[ref-complete-projection-family-for-new-member]] (the stored-vs-projected split the constructor arity reads off), [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (`RecMapEntry`'s deliberate storage decision), and [[ref-parametric-assembler-extraction]] (the symmetric-second-assembler-is-fresh-but-cheap precedent, R226/228).

### Reflection 247 (new, 2026-06-03): the producer-dual reduces one *field*, but the consumer joint demands a *bundle* — close the arity gap with a bundle assembler whose only non-pass-through field is the recursive one, and the locate's residual collapses to exactly that field

R245/R246 built the two per-level entry assemblers (`located_{entry,mapentry}_of_rec{seq,map}body`): the producer-duals that *build* a located `Rec{Seq,Map}Entry` from the inner-window deliverable. But the locate consumer joint `flowSubrangesOk_of_locators` (R243) does not consume a `RecSeqEntry` — it consumes a **`SeqLocated`**, a *four-field bundle* (`pos` / `dyck` / `wt` / `entry`). So after R245 there was a silent **arity gap** between what the dual produces (one field, `entry`) and what the joint's locator hypothesis `h_seq` demands (the whole bundle). This session closed it with `seqLocated_of_recseqbody`, a pure-packaging **bundle assembler**: `⟨h_lo, h_dyck, h_wt, located_entry_of_recseqbody …⟩`. Build green **528 jobs**, frontier sorries held at **4**, axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` (the `Classical.choice` inherited from the entry assembler's `toWellBracketed` chain).

The reusable point is *which* fields are pass-throughs and which is the residual. Three of the four `SeqLocated` fields — `pos` (`1 ≤ lo`), `dyck` (the windowed Dyck floor), `wt` (the windowed `WellTyped`) — are **window-guard pass-throughs**: the locate already holds them at each guarded window, the first as a bound, the latter two as `WellTyped_subrange`/global-Dyck restrictions. Only `entry` is recursive. So the bundle assembler's residual is **exactly the recursive field** — and because the entry assembler (R245) further reduced `entry` to the inner-window `RecSeqBody`, the *seq locator hypothesis as a whole* is now reduced to "produce the inner-window `RecSeqBody` plus the cheap derivables." This is the **producer-side mirror of R243**: where `flowSubrangesOk_of_locators` reduced the *consumer* residual (`FlowSubrangesOk`) to the locator hypotheses, `seqLocated_of_recseqbody` reduces the *producer* residual (a locator hypothesis) to the recursive sub-deliverable. Generalizing: **when a producer-dual reduces one field of a bundled deliverable, do not stop at the field — write the trivial bundle assembler immediately, because it costs nothing (the other fields are guard pass-throughs), it cannot regress (pure packaging over a proven dual), and it names the bundle's residual as precisely the recursive field, which is the only thing the recursion must actually descend on.** The map mirror `mapLocated_of_recmapbody` is the predicted next brick — and it will *not* be as clean: `MapLocated` stores six additional pair-interior primitive fields (`key_content` … `value_bracket_succ`, R232) that `located_mapentry_of_recmapbody` does not produce, so the map bundle assembler must thread them as further hypotheses. That is R246's storage asymmetry reappearing one level up — the bundled type stores more than the entry assembler delivers, so the map bundle's arity exceeds the seq bundle's by exactly the projected-not-produced pair primitives. See [[ref-producer-dual-of-consumer-joint]] (the field-level dual this bundles), [[ref-universal-packaging-is-its-own-joint]] (R243 — the consumer-side mirror this is the producer dual of), [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (the verified-but-unconsumed reshape discipline), and [[ref-mirror-constructor-arity-reads-storage]] (R246 — the storage asymmetry the map bundle will re-encounter at the field count).

### Reflection 248 (new, 2026-06-03): the map mirror of the bundle assembler completes the pair, and confirms R246's storage asymmetry is *scale-free* — the same projected-not-produced gap that shrank the entry constructor by one argument grows the bundle assembler by six hypotheses, and yields a *cleaner* axiom profile besides

R247 closed the seq-side arity gap with the bundle assembler `seqLocated_of_recseqbody` and predicted the map mirror would "not be as clean" — `MapLocated` storing six pair-interior primitives the entry assembler does not produce. This session landed `mapLocated_of_recmapbody` and the prediction held exactly. The recursive `entry` field comes via `located_mapentry_of_recmapbody` (R246); `pos`/`dyck`/`wt` are the identical window-guard pass-throughs as the seq mirror. But where the seq bundle assembler took eight hypotheses and packaged four fields, the map bundle assembler takes **fourteen** — the same eight plus the six pair-interior primitives (`h_key_content` … `h_value_bracket_succ`) typed verbatim off the `MapLocated` field signatures — because the bundled type STORES those six (the depth-0 `.key`/`.value` alternation of R232) and the entry assembler DELIVERS only the recursive `RecMapEntry`. The assembler is still a pure anonymous-constructor one-liner; it just threads the stored-but-not-produced primitives straight through. Build green **528 jobs**, frontier sorries held at **4**.

Two reusable observations sharpen R246. First, **the storage asymmetry is scale-free**: the *same* projected-not-produced distinction (R244's stored-vs-projected split) that made the entry constructor `RecMapEntry.map` *one argument shorter* than `RecSeqEntry.seq` (R246 — the map type projects `WellBracketed` rather than storing it) makes the map *bundle* assembler *six hypotheses longer* than the seq bundle (the map bundled type stores six primitives the seq bundled type does not). It manifests as a *shrink* at the entry constructor (the projected field is dropped from the call) and a *growth* at the bundle assembler (the stored fields must be threaded in) — opposite signs, one mechanism: the arity delta at any assembly layer equals THAT-layer's-bundled-type-STORES minus the-producer-DELIVERS, read off the type's field list. To author either mirror, count the target type's fields and subtract what the inner producer supplies; the remainder is precisely your hypothesis (or dropped-argument) list, and it is visible only at the assembly line. Second — a pleasant inversion of the usual "harder mirror" intuition — the map bundle is axiom **cleaner** than the seq bundle: `mapLocated_of_recmapbody` is `[propext, Quot.sound]` (no `Classical.choice`), whereas `seqLocated_of_recseqbody` carries `Classical.choice`. The reason is the *same* storage decision: the seq side threads the choice-bearing `toWellBracketed` projection chain (to supply the `WellBracketed` field `RecSeqEntry.seq` stores), while the map side never does — it projects that balance post-hoc and so never invokes the choice-bearing chain at construction. The storage decision that costs the map side six extra hypotheses *buys* it a cleaner axiom profile: storing-vs-projecting trades hypothesis count against axiom dependencies, and the trade runs in opposite directions on the two ledgers.

With both bundle assemblers landed, the producer-dual program is complete from the entry constructor up through the bundle: both per-window deliverables `SeqLocated`/`MapLocated` are now reducible to "produce the inner-window `Rec{Seq,Map}Body` (plus, on the map side, the six primitives the enclosing locate already holds)." The remaining Phase-J producer residual is the seq/map **locate recursion** itself — navigating the top-level `Rec*Body` to the inner-window `Rec*Body` at every guarded window, calling these bundle assemblers per window — fed by the **emit-producer strengthening** (`emit{List,PairList}_scans_safebody` → deliver the top-level `RecSeqBody`/`RecMapBody`), then the two base `emit_roundtrip_{sequence,mapping}_content_eq` sorries → `universal_roundtrip`. See [[ref-bundle-assembler-lifts-producer-dual]] (R247 — the seq bundle this mirrors), [[ref-mirror-constructor-arity-reads-storage]] (R246 — the storage asymmetry this confirms is scale-free), [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (`RecMapEntry`'s deliberate projection decision, the root of both the +6 hypotheses and the −`Classical.choice`), and [[ref-complete-projection-family-for-new-member]] (R244's stored-vs-projected split, the mechanism behind the arity delta at every layer).

### Reflection 249 (new, 2026-06-03): the emit-producer strengthening is itself a consumer-joint-before-producer move, and the recursive producer is a verbatim mirror of the flat one over one shared induction — only the per-entry constructor changes

With both bundle assemblers landed (R247/R248), the locate's *consumer* side is fully reduced to "produce the inner-window `Rec{Seq,Map}Body`," and the Phase-J residual splits two ways: the **locate recursion** (which navigates a top-level `Rec*Body`) and the **emit-producer strengthening** (which must *deliver* that top-level `Rec*Body` in the first place). This session opened the second. The existing producer `emitList_scans_safebody` already scans the comma-separated body of `emitList items` into a `block` and certifies the *flat* invariants `SafeBody` / `SafeBodyUnit` / `WellBracketed` / `WellTyped`; the strengthening must certify the *recursive* `RecSeqBody block` instead. The landed brick is `emitList_scans_recseqbody`.

The first reusable point: **the emit-producer strengthening is itself a consumer-joint-before-producer move (R231 family), at the emit boundary rather than the locate boundary.** The `RecSeqBody` assembler cannot be written without each item delivering a *recursive* `RecSeqEntry` — but the existing per-item handle `EmitScansInFlowBlock` discards the recursion (it carries only the flat `EntrySafe`/`WellBracketed`/content-start about the item's block; the nested `RecSeqBody interior` of a nested-sequence item is never built, and is unrecoverable from `WellBracketed` alone). So rather than first strengthen the per-item producer (the hard `Grammable`-case-split, which itself recurses through *this* assembler), name the per-item recursive deliverable as a **bare keyed hypothesis** and build the assembler on it now: `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`, defined as a strict *superset* of `EmitScansInFlowBlock` with the single extra conjunct `RecSeqEntry block` placed in the same existential — so the `RecSeqEntry` is *keyed to the same internal `block`* the scanner run produces, and the future producer supplies both flat and recursive facts from one pass. The assembler `emitList_scans_recseqbody : (∀ v ∈ items, EmitScansInFlowRecEntry v) → … RecSeqBody block` is then verified-but-unconsumed (R225): it references no sorry site, sorries held at **4**, but it retypes the residual one layer down — from "deliver the top-level `RecSeqBody`" to "deliver each item's `RecSeqEntry`."

The second reusable point: **the recursive producer is a character-for-character mirror of the flat producer over the *same* induction, differing only at the per-entry constructor.** `emitList_scans_recseqbody`'s proof is `emitList_scans_safebody`'s proof with three edits and nothing else: (i) the per-item hypothesis type `EmitScansInFlowBlock` → `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry` (so the destructure binds one extra `RecSeqEntry block` witness `h_e`/`h_e₁`); (ii) the output existential's trailing `SafeBody ∧ SafeBodyUnit` conjuncts → the single `RecSeqBody`; (iii) the two terminal constructor calls — `RecSeqBody.single block h_ne h_e h_head` in place of `SafeBody.single block h_ne h_es h_head`, and `RecSeqBody.cons block₁ feTok block_rest h_ne h_e₁ h_head h_fe h_rec_rest` in place of `SafeBody.cons …`. *Every* scanner step transports verbatim: the chain replay, the comma `.flowEntry` separator (`scanNextToken_flow_comma` + `_filtered_push`), the whitespace preprocess (`scanNextToken_preprocess_flow_ws1`), the chain lift (`ScanChainGrew_of_scanNextToken_eq` / `FlowMonoChain_of_scanNextToken_eq`), the `WellBracketed`/`WellTyped` append assembly. This is the symmetric-second-assembler economy of R226/228 (a second assembler is fresh-but-cheap when it shares the hard sub-lemmas with the first), here between the FLAT and RECURSIVE producers over a single shared induction rather than between two parallel-type halves: the flat invariant and the recursive invariant are *the same comma-separated decomposition* certified with different leaves, so the producer that builds one builds the other by swapping the leaf constructor. The axiom profile confirms the shared substrate — `emitList_scans_recseqbody` is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, identical to `emitList_scans_safebody` (the `Classical.choice` from the scanner-chain infrastructure both share). Build green **528 jobs**. Immediate next brick: the symmetric **map-body assembler `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody`** (the `RecMapBody` strengthening of `emitPairList_scans_safebody`, keyed on a per-pair `RecMapPair` deliverable — where the storage/arity asymmetry of R246/R248 reappears at the pair level), then the per-item/per-pair `Grammable` producers that close the feed (`scalar` leaf → `RecSeqEntry.scalar`, nested cases recursing through these very assemblers), then the locate recursion that consumes both. See [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (R231 — the keyed-hypothesis-before-producer discipline this applies at the emit boundary), [[ref-producer-dual-of-consumer-joint]] (the producer-side reshape family this continues), [[ref-parametric-assembler-extraction]] (R226/228 — the symmetric-assembler economy, here flat-vs-recursive over one induction), and [[ref-reduction-by-import]] (R225 — the verified-but-unconsumed retype).

The brick reproduces both R249 lessons one structural level deeper, where a flow-mapping pair `key :: (block_k ++ value :: block_v)` carries **two** `emit v` blocks (the key and the value), each one exactly what `RecSeqEntry` characterizes, so a `RecMapPair` carries two `RecSeqEntry`s. **Consumer-joint-before-producer at the emit boundary, now on both per-item feeds:** the two recursive deliverables are unrecoverable from the flat per-key/per-value handles (`EmitScansInFlowSavedKeyBlock`/`EmitScansInFlowBlock` carry only the flat saved-key/block facts), so the assembler is keyed on SUPERSET predicates — `EmitScansInFlowSavedKeyRecEntry` (new, a strict superset of `EmitScansInFlowSavedKeyBlock` with the lone extra conjunct `RecSeqEntry block`, the per-KEY twin of the seq side's `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`) for the key, and `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry` itself **reused verbatim** for the value (a value *is* an `emit v` block, so the seq side's per-item predicate serves the map side's value slot with no new definition). That reuse is itself the point: the value-side superset predicate did not have to be re-authored because the recursive characterization of "one emitted block" is shared across seq items and map values — the additive deliverable types (R242) pay off again, this time as predicate reuse rather than type reuse. **Verbatim mirror over the shared induction:** `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody`'s proof is `emitPairList_scans_safebody`'s proof with exactly the same three classes of edit R249 catalogued — strengthen the two per-item hypothesis types (binding the extra `RecSeqEntry` witnesses `h_ke`/`h_ve`), swap the output's `SafeBody (· = .key)` conjunct for `RecMapBody`, and swap the two terminal constructor calls (`RecMapBody.single`/`.cons` in place of `SafeBody.single`/`.cons`, with the per-pair `RecMapPair` assembled from the two `RecSeqEntry`s via `RecMapPair.mk` after one `cons`/`append_assoc` reassoc, in place of the per-pair `EntrySafe`). Every scanner step — the colon's placeholder→`.key` re-anchor (`scanNextToken_flow_value_block` + `List_filter_drop_succ_of_take`), the value scan, the `", "` separator, the chain lift, the `WellBracketed`/`WellTyped` glue — transports character-for-character.

The new, sharpening observation beyond R249: **the "verbatim mirror" discipline composes across two independent axes at once.** R249 mirrored flat→recursive over the seq induction; R226/228 mirrored seq→map over a fixed invariant. This brick does *both simultaneously* — it is the flat→recursive strengthening (R249's axis) applied to the map producer (R226/228's axis) — and the two axes do not interfere: the seq→map transposition was already paid for once in the flat producers (`emitList_scans_safebody` → `emitPairList_scans_safebody`), and the flat→recursive strengthening is the same leaf-swap on either, so the recursive map producer is reachable as *either* "the map transpose of `emitList_scans_recseqbody`" or "the recursive strengthening of `emitPairList_scans_safebody`" and both routes land the identical proof. The economy is multiplicative: N flat producers × the one strengthening recipe = N recursive producers, each fresh-but-cheap.

But a second observation cuts the other way and is the more useful caution: **a load-bearing scaffolding difference between the two flat producers survives the mirror untouched, and must be preserved rather than "cleaned up" to match the sibling.** The seq recursive producer (R249) *dropped* the flat-only output conjuncts (`SafeBody`/`SafeBodyUnit`) and derived its recursion's positivity (`n₃ ≥ 1`) from a chain/nonempty match. The map flat producer, by contrast, carries a `3 ≤ n` chain-length floor in its output and uses it (`omega`) to derive the tail recursion's positivity (`n_r ≥ 1`). Naïvely "mirroring" the seq recursive producer's *output shape* onto the map side — i.e. dropping `3 ≤ n` to match — would have broken the positivity derivation, because on the map side that floor is not flat-only cruft but the actual scaffolding the recursion stands on. So the map recursive producer **keeps** `3 ≤ n`, making it a *truly* verbatim mirror of the map FLAT producer (only the per-pair constructor changes, nothing in the positivity scaffolding) rather than a shape-match of the seq RECURSIVE one. The lesson: **when mirroring a strengthening, mirror the producer on the *same* axis (the flat→recursive parent), not the sibling on the *other* axis — the two siblings may carry different load-bearing scaffolding for the same sub-obligation (here, recursion positivity), and matching the wrong sibling's output shape silently removes a hypothesis a later tactic needs.** Identify what each `omega`/match in the parent proof actually consumes before deciding which output conjuncts are droppable; "this conjunct is flat-only on the seq side" does not imply "it is flat-only on the map side."

Effect: reduces "deliver the top-level `RecMapBody`" to "deliver each pair's two `RecSeqEntry`s." The next residual is the `Grammable`-case-split per-key/per-value producers — the four `EmitScans…RecEntry`-from-`Grammable` lemmas (`EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`/`EmitScansInFlowSavedKeyRecEntry` from `Grammable v inFlow`), each a strengthening of its existing flat `emit_scans_in_flow…` producer with a `RecSeqEntry`-delivering leaf, mutually recursing through these four body assemblers (`scalar` leaf → `RecSeqEntry.scalar`; nested-sequence case → `emitList_scans_recseqbody`; nested-mapping case → `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody`) — then the seq/map locate recursion that consumes the feed, then the two base `emit_roundtrip_{sequence,mapping}_content_eq` sorries → `universal_roundtrip`. See [[ref-recursive-producer-mirrors-flat-over-shared-induction]] (R249 — the seq-side parent this mirrors, and the discipline this extends to a second axis), [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (R231 — the keyed-superset-before-producer discipline applied to both per-item feeds), [[ref-parametric-assembler-extraction]] (R226/228 — the seq→map axis this composes with flat→recursive), and [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (R242 — the additive deliverable types whose payoff here is predicate *reuse* of `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry` for the value slot).

### Reflection 251 (new, 2026-06-03): the recursive-deliverable inductive's *storage* choices set the producer's recursion graph — a member that projects (not stores) its sub-structure severs a recursion edge, so the producer targeting it is strictly smaller and dependency-light

Landing the first `Grammable`-case-split emit producer, `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry : Grammable v inFlow → EmitScansInFlowRecEntry v` (commit `5ff31167`, build green **529 jobs**, frontier sorries held at **4**, axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` + pre-existing upstream `native_decide`), closes the *value half* of the emit feed: it strengthens the flat block producer `emit_scans_in_flow_block` to additionally deliver `RecSeqEntry block`, the per-item recursive deliverable that BOTH body assemblers read as a bare hypothesis — `emitList_scans_recseqbody` for every sequence item (R249), `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody` for every mapping value (R250). It is the producer-side feed those two assemblers were keyed against; with it, the per-VALUE hypothesis of both is discharged everywhere.

The mechanics are the now-familiar R249 strengthening discipline ([[ref-recursive-producer-mirrors-flat-over-shared-induction]]), one axis further down: the producer is a **verbatim mirror of `emit_scans_block_combined`'s three `block` cases** with only the per-entry `RecSeqEntry` leaf woven in — `scalar` → `RecSeqEntry.scalar` (the single token *is* the entry); `sequence` → `RecSeqEntry.seqEmpty`/`RecSeqEntry.seq`, the body block scanned by `emitList_scans_recseqbody` fed by *this* induction's own IH (per-item `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`), with an empty/nonempty split on `items.toList` because the empty sequence maps to the dedicated nullary `seqEmpty` constructor and the nonempty one to `seq` carrying the recursive `RecSeqBody`; `mapping` → `RecSeqEntry.map`. The flat conjuncts are re-derived using the **black-box flat wrappers** `emit_scans_in_flow_saved_key_block`/`emit_scans_in_flow_block` for the pair keys/values.

The sharpening observation — and the reusable lesson — is structural and was visible only once the cases were laid side by side: **the storage choices of the recursive-deliverable inductive set the shape of the producer's recursion graph.** Recall R244 ([[ref-complete-projection-family-for-new-member]]): a recursive-deliverable member *stores* exactly the fields its consumer navigation needs, *projecting* the rest. `RecSeqEntry.seq` **stores** `RecSeqBody interior` (the seq locate descends into it), but `RecSeqEntry.map` **stores only `WellBracketed interior`** — it does *not* store a recursive `RecMapBody`, because at *this* nesting level the map's interior is navigated flatly. That single storage asymmetry has a direct, non-obvious consequence for the producer: **the value producer's `mapping` case needs no map-body recursion at all** — `RecSeqEntry.map`'s only premise, `WellBracketed interior`, is already on hand from the flat mapping proof, so the case is a pure leaf with respect to the recursive deliverable. The *only* recursion in the entire value producer is the `sequence` case (through `emitList_scans_recseqbody`). The producer is therefore **self-contained: a single `Grammable` induction with NO saved-key dependency.** A member that projects rather than stores its sub-structure **severs the corresponding edge in the producer's recursion graph**, and the producer that targets that member is strictly smaller and lighter on dependencies than its storing sibling.

The corollary that orders the remaining work: **the saved-key twin is *not* symmetric to the value producer in its dependency profile, and must come second.** `emit_scans_in_flow_saved_key_rec_entry : Grammable v inFlow → EmitScansInFlowSavedKeyRecEntry v` delivers the *same* structural `RecSeqEntry` (the saved-key block is the same `emit v` token stream), so its `sequence` case *also* needs `RecSeqBody` of the items — which means it recurses through `emitList_scans_recseqbody`, whose per-item hypothesis is the **value** `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`. So the saved-key producer **depends on this value producer**, not the other way round: the value producer is the genuine base, lands first (self-contained), and the saved-key producer is the dependent next brick. Concretely this is why the value producer's own `mapping` case had to reach for the black-box flat saved-key wrapper rather than an IH — its induction motive is value-only and carries no saved-key projection, so the keys of a nested mapping *cannot* be served by the IH and *must* go through `emit_scans_in_flow_saved_key_block`. That asymmetry in where the keys come from is the same dependency edge, seen from inside the proof.

This also revises the NINETY-EIGHTH/Reflection-250 framing of the next step as "four mutually-recursive `Grammable` producers": it is more precisely **two producers** (value, then saved-key), of which the value one is a *self-contained base* and the saved-key one is its dependent. The "mutual recursion" intuition over-counted the coupling: the projection-not-storage of `RecSeqEntry.map` means neither producer recurses through the *map* body at all (`RecSeqEntry.map` is a leaf for both), so the only cross-producer dependency is the single edge saved-key → value through the seq body. Verified-but-unconsumed (R225 — [[ref-reduction-by-import]]): the producer references no sorry site, the frontier count is unchanged at 4, but the value half of the emit feed is now closed and the residual is retyped to exactly the per-key saved-key producer plus the downstream locate recursion. See [[ref-complete-projection-family-for-new-member]] (R244 — the stored-vs-projected split this reads a producer-graph consequence off of), [[ref-recursive-producer-mirrors-flat-over-shared-induction]] (R249/R250 — the strengthening discipline this instance follows), and [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (R231 — the keyed-superset feed both body assemblers were built against).

### Reflection 252 (new, 2026-06-03): the dependent member of a storage-graph-ordered producer family does not recurse on itself — its own induction hypothesis is dead, every recursive sub-need routed to the base sibling — and the emit feed is now complete

Landing the second (and last) `Grammable`-case-split emit producer, `emit_scans_in_flow_saved_key_rec_entry : Grammable v inFlow → EmitScansInFlowSavedKeyRecEntry v` (commit `69fe6722`, build green **530 jobs**, frontier sorries held at **4**, axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` + pre-existing upstream `native_decide`), closes the *key half* of the emit feed. It strengthens the flat saved-key block producer `emit_scans_in_flow_saved_key_block` to additionally deliver `RecSeqEntry block`, the per-pair *key* recursive deliverable that `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody` reads as a bare hypothesis. With the value half (R251) already landed, **every per-item hypothesis of both body assemblers is now discharged everywhere** — `emitList_scans_recseqbody` (seq items), `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody` (map keys *and* values). The emit feed is complete; the next residual is the locate recursion that *consumes* it.

Mechanically the proof is the now-familiar R249/R251 discipline once more: a **verbatim mirror of `emit_scans_block_combined`'s three `savedkey` cases** with only the per-entry `RecSeqEntry` leaf woven in — `scalar` → `RecSeqEntry.scalar`; `sequence` → `RecSeqEntry.seqEmpty`/`RecSeqEntry.seq` (empty/nonempty split, body scanned by `emitList_scans_recseqbody`); `mapping` → `RecSeqEntry.map` (leaf, premise `WellBracketed interior` already on hand). The saved-key layout scaffolding (placeholder raw-prefix tracking via `FlowMonoChain_preserves_raw_prefix`/`SimpleKeyAboveFloor`, the take-side re-anchor `h_take`, the `saveSimpleKey` restore) transports verbatim from the flat saved-key cases; it is orthogonal to the recursive-deliverable strengthening and untouched by it.

The sharpening observation — the fresh nuance of this brick — is the **empirical confirmation of R251's storage-graph prediction, plus one corollary R251 did not state explicitly: in a storage-graph-ordered producer family, the *dependent* member's own induction hypothesis is entirely DEAD.** R251 predicted (read off the constructor signatures) that the saved-key producer would *depend on* the value producer because a `sequence` scanned as a saved key has *value* body items, whose recursive deliverable is the value-side `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`, not the saved-key one. Building it confirms exactly that — and reveals the stronger fact: *none* of the saved-key producer's three cases uses its own IH. The `sequence` case routes to the black-box **value** producer `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry` (the correct deliverable for the body items); the `mapping` case routes to the black-box **flat** wrappers `emit_scans_in_flow_saved_key_block`/`emit_scans_in_flow_block` (because `RecSeqEntry.map` is a leaf needing only `WellBracketed`); the `scalar` case is a leaf. So although the producer is *written* as `induction hg with …`, the induction is vestigial — `cases hg` would do, and the IH binders are named `_ih`/`_ihk`/`_ihv` to mark them unused. The reusable lesson: **the base member of a storage-ordered producer family carries the family's *only* live self-recursion (it is the genuine fixpoint); each dependent member consumes the base as a black box and recurses on nothing of its own.** The dependency edge R251 named as "the forced black-box reach for a field the IH lacks a projection of" is here total, not partial — *every* reach is to a sibling, because *every* recursive sub-deliverable the saved-key motive would need is value-shaped, and its motive is saved-key-shaped. This sharpens [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]]: storage choices don't merely *thin* the dependent producer's recursion graph, they can *empty* it.
